open_items: ILO gateway-data-only 403 flap (standalone): now two occurrences, cycle 370 (resolved by 371, clean through 373) and cycle 322 (tail end of the cycle 321 blanket-403 episode). Both resolved within one to two cycles. Watch for a third occurrence, and specifically whether it ever persists past one cycle.

ESTAT list_dataflows timeout pattern: eighteenth episode, cycles 362-364 (three consecutive cycles, roughly 6 hours), resolved by cycle 365, clean through cycle 373. Notable as the first occurrence to persist beyond one cycle (all seventeen priors resolved within one cycle); recovered on its own without intervention. Live recheck at cycle 364 confirmed direct path genuinely slow (30.9s, 37 MB payload) but well under the 60s gateway deadline, and ruled out a network-wide issue via an ECB control request. Watch for a nineteenth episode, and specifically whether multi-cycle persistence recurs. Standing recommendation (raise deadline, stream listing, or cache parsed result) remains open as a code-change-scope fix, not actioned by this read-only routine.

ABS gateway metadata empty-error-body flap: tenth occurrence at cycle 365, resolved by cycle 366, clean through cycle 373. Ninth was cycle 321, resolved by 322. All ten occurrences have resolved within one cycle. Empty error message itself still worth fixing under code-change scope (GatewayError/next_step in monitor/checks_gateway.py).

SBS gateway DNS resolution flap: first occurrence, cycle 366 (`Temporary failure in name resolution` on gateway metadata, gateway data probe timed out), resolved by cycle 367, clean through cycle 373. Isolated to SBS; all other eleven endpoints healthy that cycle, so not a network-wide issue on the monitor's side. Same failure shape previously seen for FBOS at cycle 50 (treated as infrastructure, not provider-down). Watch for a second occurrence; escalate if it recurs.

UNICEF HTTP 429 flap: sixth occurrence cycle 346, confirmed resolved by cycle 347 as predicted, clean through cycle 373. Prior occurrences cycle 126, 178, 262, 305, 346, all resolved within one cycle. Watch for a seventh occurrence.

ILO blanket-403 provider_down episode: seventh occurrence cycle 321 (priors: 244, 251, 260, 264, 272, 281, all resolved within one cycle). This one took two cycles instead of one -- gateway_issue at 322 (gateway data probe only), fully healthy by 323, clean through 373 (the cycle 370 gateway-data-only 403 is a separate standalone occurrence of a similar shape, not a recurrence of the blanket 403 itself -- direct never failed this time). Watch for an eighth blanket-403 occurrence, and specifically whether a staggered recovery repeats or was a one-off.

ABS and ESTAT gateway_issue coincided in the same cycle (319) for the first time on record. Each pattern is independently well established; could not determine whether this reflects a shared cause or is coincidence. No second simultaneous occurrence through cycle 373. Watch for a second true same-cycle occurrence.

OECD gateway_issue 403 Forbidden episode (cycles 290-292, gateway list_dataflows and gateway data probe both HTTP 403, direct path healthy throughout): resolved by cycle 293, clean through cycle 373. First occurrence of this pattern for OECD, notable for spanning three consecutive cycles (~6h). Watch for a second occurrence; escalate for real if a future episode again spans more than one cycle.

ILO direct-path 403 flap (basic checks): tenth occurrence cycle 286, resolved by cycle 287 (one cycle, as usual), clean through cycle 320 (superseded by the blanket 403 at cycle 321, a different and more severe pattern -- see above). Prior occurrences cycle 32, 94, 159, 166, 202, 238, 244, 249, 267. Watch for an eleventh occurrence of this specific direct-only shape.

ILO references:contentconstraint broken (500) at cycle 274 resolved by cycle 275, confirmed clean through cycle 373 (reads `ignored`, not `broken`, in the current cycle's contract rows). Second occurrence overall of this assertion flapping (first was a same-cycle blip at cycle 199). Watch for a third occurrence; escalate if a future broken reading persists beyond one cycle.

ILO gateway_issue episode (cycles 268-269, gateway metadata HTTP 500 on list_dataflows, direct healthy throughout): resolved by cycle 270, clean through cycle 373. Distinct pattern from the cycle 322 and cycle 370 gateway data 403 episodes (see above): different check (metadata vs data) and different HTTP status (500 vs 403). Watch separately.

ECB contract-probe 504 flap (second pattern): constraint:availableconstraint (504 -> 404) and references:none (504 -> 200) both showed a was/now change in /api/contracts between cycle 283 and 286, verdict stayed ok throughout. No further changes list entries on these assertions through cycle 373. Not the same assertions as the cycles 182-183 references:* 504 flap (that watch item is separate, still clean). Watch for recurrence on these two assertions specifically.
ABS contract 503 flap: dialect:sdmx3 and errors:missing_artefact both returned 503 at cycle 234 only, resolved by cycle 235. Clean through cycle 373. Watch for a second occurrence.
ECB metadata 503 (provider_down): occurred cycle 199 only, resolved by cycle 200, clean through cycle 373. Watch for a second occurrence.
ABS gateway metadata 502 Bad Gateway flap: occurred cycle 198 only, resolved by cycle 199, clean through cycle 373. Watch for recurrence. Distinct from the empty-error-body flap above.
UNICEF direct-path HTTP 404 'no data found' flap: occurred cycle 197 only, resolved by cycle 198, clean through cycle 373. Watch for a second occurrence.
STATSNZ auth:listing capability_appeared, first seen cycle 60, still present at cycle 373: listing served without credentials. Still open, not re-reported since no new change.

Content-Type parameter order (charset vs version) on structure responses varies between requests. Cosmetic, verdict stays ok. Seen again on ILO's encoding:structure_xml between cycles 370 and 373. Expected to keep flapping across multiple endpoints; do not re-report unless the verdict itself changes.
IMF references:* 401 flap: first and only occurrence, cycle 161, resolved by cycle 162, clean through cycle 373. Watch for a second occurrence.
ECB references:* 504 flap (cycles 182-183 pattern): first occurrence, cycles 182-183, resolved by cycle 184, clean through cycle 373. Watch for a second occurrence.
